verses.1: And then Moses and Aaron came and said to Pharaoh, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, has said, ‘Send my people away from me, and they will worship me in the wilderness.’”
verses.2: And Pharaoh said, “Who is Jehovah that I should listen to him and send Israel away? I do not know Jehovah, and I certainly will not send Israel away.”
verses.3: And the gods of the Israelites said, “It is called a pilgrimage for us. Let us go through the desert for three days, and then we will worship our God Yehovah. Otherwise, they might harm us with their words or their actions.”
verses.4: And the king of Egypt said to them, “Why do Moses and Aaron try to stop the people from doing what they want? Go ahead and suffer your punishment.”
verses.5: And Pharaoh said, “Now these people are numerous. They have been freed from their sufferings.”
verses.6: And on that day, Pharaoh commanded the scribes and officials to do as he said.
verses.7: Do not gather them together to make mats for the people. Instead, let them go and make their own mats by themselves.
verses.8: And when you prepare the utensils they use to make the bread, place them on top of it. Do not remove anything from them. For they are meant to be used for worshiping our God.
verses.9: May the labor be done with care, and may people do it properly. Let them not be saved by false words.
verses.10: And the officers and soldiers of the people went out and said to the people, “As Pharaoh has said, I will not give you any wages.”
verses.11: Go ahead, take some wood with you. You will find that nothing can be left undone in your work.
verses.12: And the people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt, in search of a place to live.
verses.13: And those who do evil deeds will say, “Your actions are like those of a day that has passed.” Just as it was in the past.
verses.14: And the priests of Israel, who were under Pharaoh’s command, said, “Why do you not follow the laws? You should be like the Levites who are dedicated to serving God.”
verses.15: And the priests of Israel came forward and cried out to Pharaoh, “What are you doing to your servants?”
verses.16: “There is no one given to serve your gods. Your people say, ‘Do what you want.’ But look! Your servants are destroyed, and their sins are punished.”
verses.17: And Nirpim said, “You are worthless people. Therefore, you say, ‘Let us go and worship Jehovah.’”
verses.18: And now, go and serve. But do not expect to be given anything in return. Instead, let them give you some seeds in exchange.
verses.19: And the priests of Israel saw them in a bad light. They said, “Do not be removed from among your people on this day.”
verses.20: And they fell upon Moses and Aaron, as they were standing to read from the Torah after leaving Pharaoh’s house.
verses.21: And they said to them, “The LORD will see you and punish those who brought this stench before Pharaoh’s eyes and before his servants’ eyes. They will be killed by their own hands.”
verses.22: And Moses sat down before Jehovah and said, “Lord, why have you done this to this people? Why did You send me?”
verses.23: And from that time on, I came before Pharaoh to speak on your behalf. But you did not do what was right for this people. You did not save your own people.
